title: ggctl Report
description: The one document ggctl writes to standard output with --format json, for every command that does not write an artifact. exitCode and outcome are the process exit status and its stable name. Diagnostics are value-free: a stable family.reason code, fixed message text, an optional fixed hint, a documentation anchor, and at most one location: the 1-based position of the command-line argument concerned, or a bundle-relative file name with a JSON Pointer built from member names the bundle reader defines and a 1-based line and column, or the position of the argument naming a document that is not a bundle file (the init answers) with a JSON Pointer and a line and column, or the position of the option naming an environment file (--env, --against-env) with a 1-based line, or the 1-based position of a backup archive's entry and of the earlier entry it clashes with; a diagnostic about an environment file also names the inventoried setting it concerns (field) and the configuration compiler rule that refused it (rule) where there are any; never an argument, token, URL, path, document value, server response, or library error. A published diagnostic code never changes meaning; renaming or removing one requires a new report version. An argument error found before a command runs writes no report (exit 2, standard error only).

apiVersion.description: Exact document version. No other version, prefix, or spelling is accepted.

code.description: The stable family.reason code. docs/ggctl.md lists every ggctl code by family, docs/configuration-bundles.md every bundle reader code, and docs/archive-admission.md every archive admission code.

message.description: Fixed text chosen by the code.

hint.description: Fixed guidance chosen by ggctl, never derived from input.

argument.description: The 1-based position of the command-line argument after ggctl.

file.description: The bundle-relative name of the file concerned; it passed the portable file-name grammar.

pointer.description: An RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into the file's document, built from member names the reader defines and array indices; empty for the document as a whole.

argument.description: The 1-based position of the command-line argument naming the document, which is not a bundle file: the init answers. Its path is never echoed.

pointer.description: An RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into the document, built from member names the reader defines and array indices; empty for the document as a whole.

argument.description: The 1-based position of the option naming the environment file. Its path is never echoed.

line.description: The 1-based line of the environment file concerned: for a compiler finding, the line of the effective (last) assignment of its setting.

entry.description: The 1-based position of the backup archive entry the archive admission rules refused. Its name is never echoed.

conflictsWith.description: For a duplicate, case-colliding or conflicting entry, the 1-based position of the earlier entry it clashes with.

field.description: The inventoried gateway setting an environment file diagnostic concerns, as the configuration compiler's inventory spells it. A key outside the inventory is never named.

created.description: The archive is at --output and passed every check of ggctl backup verify. Nothing is at --output otherwise.

backup.description: The backup written, once it verified.

verified.description: Every check passed: the archive admission rules, the manifest, every entry's SHA-256, the archive's digest, SQLite's integrity check and description of each database, and the ledger's verification.

restored.description: The state directory holds the backup's stores and the restore marker the next gateway start records, after every check of ggctl backup verify and the restore's own passed in a staging directory and the staging directory was renamed into its place.

targetUnchanged.description: Present when nothing was restored: whether the state directory was left as it was, which it is unless restore.rollback_failed was reported.

restoreId.description: The restore's opaque ID, which its marker and the config.restore_detected event carry.

replaced.description: The state directory held stores, which --replace-existing-state named and the restore replaced.

backupStoreId.description: The store a refusal concerns, when it concerns one.

backup.description: A backup as its GatewayBackup manifest describes it (gateway-backup.v1alpha1.schema.json): fixed names, versions, counts and opaque revision IDs, never a path or a store's content.

createdAtMs.description: Milliseconds since the Unix epoch, as the writer stamped it.

stores.description: Every store of the state-directory layout, in the layout's order.

entry.description: The entry holding the store: its own file, or the file of an earlier store it was another name for.

ledger.description: Present when the configuration revision ledger is included.

schemas.description: The document versions this ggctl publishes schemas for.

server.description: Present only with --server. compatible is true only when the server's capability document was read and is one this ggctl implements; gatewayVersion appears when the server stated a well-formed one, and capabilities only when compatible.

capabilities.description: The server's GatewayCapabilities document as ggctl read it; gateway-capabilities.v1alpha1.schema.json is its schema.

valid.description: No stage of the bundle reader found an error, the production policy and tools validators included, or, for an environment file, the file was read, every line is blank, a comment or an assignment, no key is assigned twice under --strict, and the configuration compiler accepted it; a warning under --warnings-as-errors changes the exit code, not this.

environment.description: What a report says about an environment file: the inventoried gateway settings it assigns and how many other keys it assigns, which are never named, and how many assignments repeat an earlier key. Never a value or the file's path.

settings.description: The inventoried settings the file assigns, in the order the configuration compiler reads them.

configRule.description: The stable name of the configuration compiler rule that refused a setting (gateway_config::compiler::diagnostic::ConfigRule). value is the refusal of one setting's own value; every other rule relates settings. docs/ggctl.md lists every rule.

bundle.description: What the bundle's manifest declares, present once the manifest was read. sourceDigest, the deployment's sha256 and profile, and each bundled resource's sha256 appear only when every stage passed. Names, versions, and digests only; never document content.

sourceDigest.description: An integrity value over the framed manifest bytes, not a signature.

productionValidator.description: For a document the bundle supplies, once the bundle was read with no error: passed, the production validator the gateway's loader runs accepted it. not_run is deprecated: earlier releases, which could not run the production validators, reported it, and no release reports it now.

check.description: One offline doctor check. severity is error for a required check, whose failure fails the doctor, and warning for advice; skipped never counts as pass. reason is a bundle reader code, an environment file or configuration compiler code, or a doctor reason. docs/ggctl.md lists every check and reason.

durationMs.description: Checks drawn from the one bundle reader run report that run's duration.

created.description: The bundle is at the --output directory. It was read back with the bundle reader and the production policy and tools validators before it was moved there.

topology.description: Present once the answers were read. standalone: the bundle supplies its policy and tools; cluster: the server's control planes do.

operator.description: Present once the answers were read: whether the policy holds the generated operator role.

bundle.description: The bundle as the reader read it back, once it was written.

valid.description: The bundle reader accepted BUNDLE, with the production policy and tools validators, so it could be converted.

bundle.description: BUNDLE, once its manifest was read.

from.description: BUNDLE's document version, once it was read.

to.description: The document version converted to, present only when --to named one this ggctl implements and the conversion was planned.

changed.description: A conversion step ran, so the converted files differ from BUNDLE's. Always false while greengateway.dev/v1alpha1 is the only version.

written.description: The converted bundle is at the --output directory. Always false with --in-place, which writes nothing.

converted.description: The bundle written to --output as the reader read it back.

valid.description: Every check of the bundle reader except the comparison of each referenced file with its pin passed, the production policy and tools validators included, so the bundle could be pinned.

bundle.description: BUNDLE as its manifest declares it, once the manifest was read: never a digest or the profile, since its pins are what is being replaced.

files.description: Each referenced file's pin, the deployment document's first, once the bundle could be pinned; empty otherwise.

changed.description: A pin differed from its file's SHA-256, so bundle.yaml had to be rewritten.

written.description: The new bundle.yaml is in place; only the changed pins' digits differ from the old one. false when every pin already matched.

pinned.description: The bundle as the reader read it back with every check, its pins included, present only when it was exactly the bundle that was pinned; its sourceDigest is the bundle's new identity.

file.description: The bundle-relative file name; it passed the portable file-name grammar.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the file's exact bytes as read, which the new bundle.yaml pins.

valid.description: Both sides were read with no error and could be compared, so they were: two bundles, read with the production policy and tools validators included and compared by the documents those validators built, or two environment files. An environment file and a bundle are never compared (diff.not_comparable).

bundle.description: BUNDLE, the candidate, once its manifest was read.

against.description: The --against bundle, the base, once its manifest was read.

environment.description: The --env file, the candidate, once it was parsed.

againstEnvironment.description: The --against-env file, the base, once it was parsed.

diff.description: The changes from the base to the candidate, present when valid.

valid.description: The bundle reader accepted BUNDLE strictly, the production policy and tools validators included: an entry the manifest does not reference is an error.

seeded.description: The state directory's new ledger holds the bundle as its first revision, desired and not active.

bundle.description: BUNDLE, once its manifest was read.

ledger.description: The new ledger's pointer, once seeded.

verified.description: Every check of the ledger passed, read-only: location and permissions, page structure, schema, every record and its hash, the chain, every document and the pointer.

rolledBack.description: A new forward revision restores the target's content, held to the production policy and tools validators when it was compiled again.

plan.description: The rollback as the revision service planned it, once planned.

revision.description: The revision appended, once rolled back.

ledger.description: The ledger's pointer, once rolled back.

ledgerCorruption.description: Present when the ledger failed verification: the class of what was found (docs/configuration-ledger.md#verification).

revisions.description: How many revisions the ledger holds.

desired.description: The newest revision, which is always the desired one.

active.description: The revision a gateway last compiled and activated; null until one has.

restartPending.description: The desired revision is not the active one: a gateway starting from the ledger activates it.

ledgerRevision.description: One revision as the ledger records it, without its actor's identity or any document content.

rollbackOf.description: For a rollback, the revision whose content it restores.

activation.description: When the revision takes effect. A seed and an offline rollback are restart: no gateway is running to activate them.

recordedAtMs.description: Milliseconds since the Unix epoch, as the writer stamped it.

appliedOnline.description: The revision records the online request it was applied under; false for a seed and for an offline command's revision.

base.description: The desired revision the rollback was planned against.

target.description: REVISION, as the ledger holds it.

riskCodes.description: The change's risk codes, sorted: each must be named with --acknowledge. Every code is acknowledgeable offline, risk.admin_access_path_removed included.

unacknowledged.description: The risk codes --acknowledge did not name.

requiredPermissions.description: The union of permissions the change would need online. An offline command checks none: filesystem access to the state directory is already full control of the deployment.

activation.description: How the change would take effect online; null when it changes nothing. The revision an offline rollback appends is restart-class whatever this is.

diffResult.description: A semantic diff between two compiled configurations, as gateway-config computes it (docs/semantic-diff.md); ggctl diff reports it for two bundles. Value-free by construction: only booleans, fixed words and numbers are ever shown; every other value is withheld, and a secret, secret reference or locator is reported only as a changed reference.

severity.description: The highest severity of any risk code, none when no change carries one.

riskCodes.description: Every change's risk codes, sorted and without duplicates.

changes.description: One entry per field that differs, ordered by section and field.

riskCode.description: A stable risk code. A published code never changes meaning; renaming or removing one requires a new report version.

field.description: The stable field identifier: an environment setting name for a deployment setting, or a dotted document path for a bundle or resource member.

class.description: How the change can take effect (ADR-0008, Change classes).

effect.description: loosened when any facet weakens a control, otherwise unknown when no detector can tell, otherwise tightened or neutral.

entries.description: For a collection: how many entries were added, removed and changed. Entry names are never reported.

shownValue.description: A boolean, a fixed word, a number, or the word unbounded.

digest.description: An ADR-0004 digest: sha256: and 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits.

code.description: A stable code a gateway reported, in lowercase snake segments.

refusal.description: A request the gateway refused: its HTTP status, its stable reason and its structured request diagnostics (a stable code, a JSON Pointer into the request and the gateway's fixed message). The free-text error and errors members of the answer are never repeated.

valid.description: Present once the gateway judged the document: the gateway's policy validator found no error, its cross-resource checks included.

diagnostics.description: The validator's diagnostics, as POST /policy/validate reported them.

resourceSnapshot.description: The resources the cross-resource checks read.

status.description: The run's status, once it completed. Only passed exits 0.

results.description: The gateway's policy-test-results.v1 report, as it answered it (docs/policy-tests.md).
The gateway's policy-simulation-results.v1 document, as it answered it (docs/policy-simulation.md).

job.description: The gateway's policy-replay-job.v1 job, as it last answered it (docs/policy-replay.md).

discarded.description: For a cancellation: true when the job had finished and was discarded.

verdict.description: integrity_valid when the package is exactly its RFC 8785 bytes and every artifact its manifest names is present, of its defined media type and schema version, and of the stated size and ADR-0004 digest; not_verified for a version, artifact or signature claim this ggctl does not verify.

signature.description: No signature is verified: packages are unsigned.

trusted.description: Integrity shows the package is unchanged since its manifest was computed, not who computed it.

sourceDigest.description: The ADR-0004 source digest of the file's bytes (application/vnd.greengateway.policy-evidence+json, policy-evidence.v1).

report.description: The report's own completeness statement, for a package whose integrity verified.
